result.title: PRIO: Pre-trained Representation for Interactive Objects in 4D Worlds
result.summary: 3D worlds can now be captured, reconstructed, and generated at scale, yet the objects in them stay still: a pressed pillow does not compress, and a pulled door does not swing. Bringing these objects into interactive 4D world models requires a representation of how they can move, deform, and respond physically to user actions in real time. We present PRIO, a pre-trained representation for interactive objects. Given static geometry, PRIO predicts an object-specific configuration space in a single forward pass. This space provides generalized coordinates for Lagrangian mechanics, allowing physical laws and user actions to govern motion. Configurations are linear in these coordinates, allowing the quantities needed by the dynamics to be precomputed. Dynamics then run at interactive rates without further network inference. Pre-trained on diverse 4D trajectories, PRIO learns priors over object configurations that generalize to unseen shapes. It supports meshes, point clouds, and 3D Gaussians, bringing objects in reconstructed and generated scenes into interaction. We demonstrate its use in real-to-sim workflows and robot manipulation. In addition, compared with existing 4D generation methods, PRIO generates dynamics faster and follows user actions more faithfully.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 PRIO，从静态几何出发一次前向预测物体特有的配置空间，为拉格朗日力学提供广义坐标，使物体在用户动作下按物理律实时运动、无需再跑网络推理，并支持网格、点云与 3D Gaussians。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「一次前向预测紧凑状态空间、随后在该空间内低成本迭代更新」的结构与 LVR 关心的 latent 状态表示和推理期计算成本解耦有形式上的相似，可供核查状态空间设计与动态更新分工的借鉴，但任务场景（物理仿真、机器人操作）与视觉语言推理相距较远。
